transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Helios CTO), Maya Lin (Helios ML Eng), Luca Rossi (Helios Infra)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on model selection tradeoffs for Helios' multilingual customer support assistant. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, required context window, tool-calling for retrieval + function calls, and security requirements (SOC2, SAML, KMS). Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing + security docs; POC to benchmark Llama3/Mistral/Falcon variants on 32k and 64k contexts.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain points
- Model context length needs (32k vs 64k+), multilingual quality (EN/ES/FR/DE/JP), and hallucination mitigation
- Tool-calling and retrieval: embeddings vs RAG connectors, function-calling support
- Deployment mode: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem constraints)
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS, audit logs

Action items summary (see metadata for owners)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex at Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:09] Samir Patel: Hey Alex, good thanks. Quick intro, I'm Samir, CTO at Helios. Maya is our ML lead, Luca is infra.
[00:16] Maya Lin: Hi all.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Great, thanks. Agenda for today is to understand your workload — model selection, context length, multilingual, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense.
[00:30] Samir Patel: Yes, main use case is customer support assistant across EN, ES, FR and some JP. We're doing retrieval over our KB, and we need function calling for actions (ticket create, lookup). Latency target is sub 300ms p50 for short queries, but some long context sessions okay at higher latency.
[00:45] Maya Lin: Also context windows matter — we have tickets that reference up to 40k tokens when you include long threads and attachments. We don't do attachments in LLM directly yet but want the model to see long convo history.
[01:00] Alex Park: Okay — sounds like context length is a critical driver. For 40k you'd be looking at models with 32k+ windows; we can route to 32k models or 64k variants depending on the model. Are you open to chunking older history into embeddings and retrieval?
[01:15] Maya Lin: We are. But prefer native long context for the few sessions where full history is helpful — like appeals or escalations. So a hybrid approach.
[01:25] Priya Nair: Makes sense. From a model perspective we usually evaluate Llama3-family, Mistral, and Falcon variants for open models. Each has differences: latency, multilinguality, and tool-calling reliability. We can run bench comparisons on Hosted or Dedicated.
[01:40] Luca Rossi: What's the tradeoff if we go Hosted vs Dedicated? Security-wise we want VPC peering or Private if required.
[01:47] Alex Park: Hosted is fastest to get started (and cost-effective for variable volume). Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput — good if you have steady high qps and want isolation. Private (VPC/private deployment) is for strict compliance — you run in your VPC or on-prem with our control plane options.
[02:05] Samir Patel: We do have requirements around audit logs and KMS for encryption. SOC2 and SAML SSO are musts. How mature are those in Redwood Private?
[02:14] Priya Nair: We have SOC2 docs and SSO integrations; Private adds customer-managed KMS and VPC options plus extended audit logs. I'll share the SOC2 and KMS notes after the call.
[02:25] Maya Lin: For model selection — we need multilingual fidelity. In your experience which open models handle Japanese and European languages best?
[02:33] Priya Nair: Mistral 7B/Chat variants do well on European languages; Llama3 chat models generalize well; some Falcon variants have strong token throughput but can lag on less common languages. We'll include a multilingual eval in the POC. Also tokenizer behavior matters — sometimes segmentation impacts Japanese.
[02:50] Samir Patel: Also we want deterministic function-calling behavior for ticket create — prefer models with stable structured output.
[02:58] Alex Park: Right — we support structured function calling across model families, but the reliability varies. Our Redwood Console can validate responses and we can add deterministic parsers in the tool layer. For the POC we can test function-calling on the models you care about.
[03:15] Maya Lin: Any recommendations on quantization or perf settings? We care about latency, but also cost.
[03:20] Priya Nair: Quantization helps on Dedicated/private to reduce memory footprint — 4-bit/8-bit tradeoffs. For Hosted, we have optimized kernels and batching; we can tune batch windows to hit your latency SLOs. We'll recommend quantization profiles per model in the report.
[03:36] Luca Rossi: Network — if we do Dedicated with VPC peering, is there egress? How do you handle data-in-flight and at-rest?
[03:45] Alex Park: Data in transit is TLS, at rest is encrypted; Private gives you customer-managed KMS for keys. For Dedicated we can do VPC peering and private networking; I'll have Priya send the network checklist; some customers keep inference data ephemeral for compliance.
[03:58] Samir Patel: For the POC we'd like to test 32k and 64k contexts and compare hallucination rates and latency across models. Also compare token-cost.
[04:09] Priya Nair: Agreed. We'll prepare a benchmark spreadsheet: latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, hallucination metric on your eval prompts, multilingual accuracy. Host it shared so we can iterate.
[04:20] Maya Lin: Awesome. Timeline — we want to decide in ~3 weeks, start POC next week if possible.
[04:26] Alex Park: We can aim to start the POC next week; I'll send a proposed plan. Any blockers for Hosted?
[04:31] Samir Patel: None immediate, but procurement wants pricing comparisons and security docs. If we do Dedicated we need buy-in from infra for GPU sizing.
[04:40] Priya Nair: Noted — we'll include Dedicated sizing options. Also, if you want Private on-prem, that has longer lead time (we'll detail that).
[04:49] Luca Rossi: For on-prem, what's the recommended GPU for 64k context? Memory becomes big.
[04:54] Priya Nair: Yes, 64k pushes memory; recommended setups vary by model and quantization — typically A100s or H100s with optimized kernels, and we can provide exact footprints in the sizing doc.
[05:05] Maya Lin: Regarding embeddings and retrieval — we have an existing Pinecone setup. Any issues integrating?
[05:11] Alex Park: We integrate with common vector DBs — Pinecone, Milvus, etc. For tight latency, local caches and prefix KV caching help.
[05:19] Samir Patel: Competitors question — we've seen demos from OpenAI and Anthropic; what are Redwood's edge cases?
[05:25] Alex Park: Our differentiation is production-first runtime: predictable latency, batching controls, model routing, Dedicated capacity, and Private options for strict compliance. We'll show concrete numbers in the POC.
[05:38] Maya Lin: Ok. Quick clarification: function-calling + retrieval — do any models handle both better natively?
[05:45] Priya Nair: Some chat-tuned models handle function calling better; tool-calling reliability can be address in the orchestration layer (Redwood Console) with validation, retries. We'll test end-to-end.
[05:57] Samir Patel: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side for next steps?
[06:00] Maya Lin: I'll collate prompts, bilingual test cases, and send them.
[06:04] Luca Rossi: I'll check VPC peering possibility and share network constraints.
[06:07] Alex Park: Great. We'll follow up with pricing, SOC2 docs, a POC plan and bench spreadsheet.
[06:12] Priya Nair: I'll include model recommendations and quantization profiles for 32k/64k.
[06:16] Samir Patel: Thanks, all.
[06:18] Alex Park: Thanks everyone — recap: Redwood sends pricing + security docs + POC plan, Helios sends sample prompts, target contexts, and network constraints.
[06:27] (meeting ends)

References shared during call:
- Redwood POC benchmark template (link: https://redwood.ai/poctemplate)
